top.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
top.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that . top.title: His father's death nearly ended his boxing career. Now he's rebuilding it beneath Sixth and Market
top.description: Professional boxers Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic, left, and Lawrence King spar at Abaddon Fight Club Gym in San Francisco. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) In the summer of 2025, Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic was ready to quit boxing. Widely regarded as the best fighter to come out of San Francisco in a generation, the light heavyweight was a nine-time national amateur boxing champion, with more than 100 fights to his name. He was 9-1 since turning pro. At 27, he was in his prime. But in August of that year, his desire to keep fighting disappeared when his father, Sheldon Callum, overdosed on fentanyl at the Western Hotel on Leavenworth Street in the Tenderloin . Callum died just a few blocks from the Turk Street apartment building where the family lived when Mahmutovic was a kid. In losing Callum, Mahmutovic lost not just his dad, but the man who had coached him since he started fighting competitively at age 8. That's nearly two decades of predawn workouts and late-night drives, convention centers and casinos, drafty high school gyms and damp basement fight clubs. The road had taken them from the Tenderloin to Reno, Kansas City to Albuquerque, Tijuana to Ukraine. Professional boxer Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic rests after a 12-round sparring session. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) Boxing is a hard business, and with his dad gone Mahmutovic wasn't sure he had the heart to keep going. He had a wife and two young sons to take care of. He had a full-time job installing and testing fire alarm systems. It wasn't like he was getting rich in the boxing ring. He had rent to pay in Oakland. Meanwhile at Abaddon Fight Club, a bare-bones basement boxing gym at Sixth and Market streets in San Francisco, Jason "JP" Peterson wondered about Mahmutovic. Peterson had opened the gym in 2023, and in the months before Callum died, Mahmutovic had started stopping by the gym to work out or spar. Now Mahmutovic was nowhere to be found. "All of a sudden he disappeared," Peterson said. "He deleted everything off his social media. I was like, ‘Bro, what are you doing?' He was kind of like, ‘Look, man, it's not the same anymore.' His exact words were, ‘I don't know if I want to do this anymore.'" Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic has his gloves tied by coach Jason Peterson before sparring at Abaddon Fight Club. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. top.description: Arsenal stars given FPL ban after team news leak Arsenal players, like many professional footballers and supporters, enjoy participating in the popular Fantasy Premier League (FPL) game. However, the game has reportedly become an unexpected source of team news, prompting Mikel Arteta to introduce restrictions on how his players use it. The Gunners do not deliberately reveal their starting line ups, but selecting themselves in their FPL teams can provide supporters and opposing clubs with clues about their availability and potential involvement in upcoming matches. This became an issue ahead of Arsenal’s game against Liverpool at Anfield . Christos Tzolis had only returned to training a few days before the encounter, and there was considerable uncertainty over whether he would be fit enough to start. However, the Greek star selected himself in his FPL team and even made himself captain, suggesting that he expected to feature from the beginning. This reportedly did not go down well with Arteta, who wants to keep his selection decisions private until matchday. Arteta introduces FPL restrictions According to the Daily Mail , Arteta has now banned his players from selecting themselves in their respective FPL teams. The restriction also means Arsenal players are no longer allowed to include their teammates in their fantasy squads. The reported decision is intended to prevent accidental leaks of team information through the popular fantasy football competition. Even without deliberately sharing confidential information, players could provide useful clues about the manager’s selection plans through their choices. For a club competing at the highest level, keeping opponents guessing about the starting line up can be an important part of match preparation. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Tzolis makes changes to his fantasy team The report also reveals that Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his FPL team ahead of the Gunners’ next fixture . That change appears to reflect the new restriction introduced by Arteta and suggests that the players have been made aware of the manager’s expectations. Although fantasy football is generally regarded as harmless entertainment, the situation demonstrates how even small details can attract attention when professional footballers participate in public competitions. top.description: Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan will look for ways to make a dent in a Minnesota Vikings defense that leads the NFL with 37 sacks when the teams meet Sunday night in Mexico City. (John Froschauer/Associated Press) The last time Brock Purdy played a Brian Flores-led defense, he was in awe. On Sept. 15, 2024, right after losing 23-17 to the Minnesota Vikings , the San Francisco 49ers quarterback approached their defensive coordinator at midfield. "Your scheme is crazy!" Purdy told Flores, as picked up by surrounding microphones, after he was sacked a season-high six times and blitzed on 52% (23 of 44) of his dropbacks. Purdy still threw for 319 yards that afternoon, but he never looked settled. The 49ers went 3-for-13 on third and fourth down. They put together only one scoring drive before the fourth quarter. And yet, if Purdy thought Flores designed an aggressive scheme back in 2024, the tape Purdy has been watching ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 game against the Vikings in Mexico City must look extraterrestrial. Minnesota, which blitzed on a league-high 39.9% of dropbacks two seasons ago, has blitzed on a league-high 69.3% of dropbacks this season. That's nearly 30% higher than the next-most blitz happy team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Vikings' pressure rate (49.8%) and sack rate (12%) also comfortably lead the NFL. Flores does it with a sense of chaotic unpredictability, too: Five Vikings have recorded at least three sacks this season. "He's more unique than all the other 31 guys. He's the one guy who commits to this, and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said of Flores. "A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure is really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are (the plays) where everything can come. When you play against Brian, it's 70 straight plays of that." "They're going to throw a lot at you, right?" Niners offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak added. "They're playing in this scheme where they're throwing different blitzes at you, different coverages, but the way they're tied together and the way that they can all play so fast and decisively, that's what makes this an elite defense to me. I think if you tried to go and install this defense in a new place, it would take a while to get a group of guys to play the way they play. They're violent." top.description: Jonathan Loáisiga - NY Yankees | © Instagram /@loaisiga_43 Jonathan Loáisiga is headed back to the Bronx after agreeing to a two-year, $18 million deal with the Yankees, with a 2029 club option, according to ESPN’s Jorge Castillo . The Nicaraguan spent eight years with New York before the team declined his club option last offseason, making him a free agent. Loáisiga later signed a minor league contract with the Diamondbacks and earned a spot on the 2026 opening-day roster after an impressive spring training. When news of the 32-year-old’s reported return to New York broke on social media, fans shared their reactions. Loáisiga has had an injury-ridden history in the MLB, starting with a shoulder injury in 2019. The injury resurfaced in 2022 and 2023, followed by elbow injuries from 2023 to 2025. He also had a back injury in 2025, and missed a large chunk of the 2024 season with a torn UCL. “Like why is this even an idea lol,” one fan commented. Loáisiga appeared in a career-high 67 games for the Diamondbacks last season, finishing with a 7-3 record, a 2.42 ERA, 48 strikeouts, and a 1.03 WHIP over 67 innings. It was a clear resurgence for the injury-prone reliever, who last posted a sub-3 ERA in 2021 with the Yankees, going 9-4 in 57 appearances. Loáisiga has made only 11 starts in his big-league career, but his work as a reliever has been eye-catching. Still, his multiple IL stints over the years will be a concern for the Bronx Bombers. Both were projected to earn $2.3 million through arbitration. New York tendered contracts to its other seven arbitration-eligible players: José Caballero, Luis García Jr., Clarke Schmidt, Anthony Volpe, Ryan Weathers, Heliot Ramos, and Austin Wells. Born in Delhi and a team-mate of India captain Shubman Gill in Indian domestic cricket, Chaudhary only switched to representing Australia after the Covid pandemic meant he got stuck in Brisbane celebrating his 24th birthday. Progression through Australian club and domestic cricket followed - plus a stint working in a Mexican restaurant - before the 30-year-old played his standout performance to date in his fourth international at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Helping restrict England to 187-9 despite Harry Brook's fireworks in smashing 65 off 28 balls, Chaudhary took 2-21 with his mystery spin and then hit 66 to steer Australia within 20 runs of victory. The elegant right-hander appeared to anger both Liam Dawson and Sam Curran during his knock and the MCG crowd loudly booed England as the tourists slowed the game in the final moments. "You always know it is going to be a big game against England so there is going to be some chirp," said Chaudhary. Curran was left with 11 to defend from the last over but all-rounder Jack Edwards finished with 25 not out as Australia completed their highest chase on home soil with three wickets and one ball remaining. The win offers some relief to Australia - an XI featuring a host of new faces putting aside the ongoing sandpaper scandal to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. England can level the contest in Gold Coast on Tuesday. top.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
top.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. NC State fans knew it when they pressured A.D. Boo Corrigan to hire him. It should not have surprised anyone that he used the Wolfpack as a quick way station before bolting back to LSU at the first opportunity. LSU fans know this too. They simply love a rogue, which is why they embraced the return of the Harold Hill of college basketball. top.title: Preview | Lazio-Juventus Women
top.description: Preview | Lazio-Juventus Women The Women’s First Team return to Serie A Women action with a Matchday 8 game against Lazio in Rome. Having beaten OH Leuven and secured a place in the next round of the UEFA Women’s Champions League in midweek, the Bianconere now want to build on their improving league form. Let’s get up to speed ahead of the game with some pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS Juventus are one of four teams to have scored at least five goals against Lazio in a Serie A match (alongside Fiorentina, Inter and Milan), but they are the only ones to have done so on two occasions: a 5-0 home win on 13 November 2021 and a 5-1 away win on 24 April 2022. Juventus have won their last three Serie A matches and have not managed four consecutive wins since the period between November 2024 and January 2025. Juventus are the team with the most sequences of at least 10 passes in this Serie A season, both in total (105, at least 40 more than any other side in the competition) and in terms of those that have led to a shot or a touch in the opposition’s penalty area (18). Alba Redondo has been directly involved in at least one goal in all seven Serie A matches she has played so far (6 goals + 3 assists); since Opta began recording key passes (2020/21), only one player has reached eight: Tabitha Chawinga with Inter between December 2022 and March 2023 – Manuela Giugliano could also equal the record this matchday, having been involved in at least one goal in each of the first seven matchdays. Remina Chiba, who proved decisive with a goal and two assists in the last matchday against Inter, has been involved in five goals (3G+2A) in this Serie A season, all as a substitute; the last Juventus player to have scored at least four goals as a substitute in a single season was Joe Echegini (four in 2023/24). UWCL | Gallery | Juventus-OH Leuven OPPOSITION FOCUS Lazio have yet to win a match in this Serie A season (3 draws, 4 defeats) and could fail to secure a single victory in any of their first eight matches played in a single season for the second time in their history, following the 2021/22 season (8 defeats). Lazio have drawn their last three home league matches 0-0 and, since Serie A came under the management of the FIGC (1986/87), no team has ever recorded four consecutive goalless home draws in the competition. The first of the three goals scored by Manuela Sciabica in Serie A came against Juventus on 15 January 2023 whilst playing for Sassuolo; the 20-year-old Biancoceleste player is one of four midfielders born in 2006 or later to have made more than five appearances (six) in Serie A.

nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. nigeria.title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
nigeria.description: Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election. The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership. “I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election. “This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. “We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership. “This is in our collective interest,” he added. The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport. “Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said. He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared. “His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said. Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election. Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him. nigeria.title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
nigeria.description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage. Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people. “It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media. “Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred. The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said. Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located. Another 32 municipalities also reported damage. This handout picture released by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defence Department shows the damage caused by strong winds in Tupancireta, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, on November 20, 2026. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm. “We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha. Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm. Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city. State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster. Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes. nigeria.title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle. “The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.” Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. nigeria.title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
nigeria.description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. He said his presence demonstrated the enduring bonds of brotherhood, friendship and mutual respect among traditional rulers in Nigeria, irrespective of ethnic and regional differences. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. sports.description: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg has been in the headlines for one reason or another since joining the Golden State Warriors. First, it was his altercation with Luka Doncic on the court that caught everyone’s attention. Then, his incredible run of form made him a fan favourite. Now, Lendeborg and the Warriors are struggling, and that poor run seems to be affecting the rookie a lot more than it should. Coach Steve Kerr has claimed that Lendeborg needs to stop. Steve Kerr tells Yaxel Lendeborg to stop being ‘too emotional’ Lendeborg wears his heart on his sleeve, and that is a good trait to have. That brought the best out of the 24-year-old early on in the season, but he has struggled in recent games, much like his teammates. Lendeborg has been affected so much that he decided to cut his hair and has looked beyond dejected on the bench in more than one game. Kerr has noticed that, and he has urged his rookie to stop being too emotional. He said on 95.7 The Game: “He is (down on himself). I think it’s actually been discussed publicly. He hung the towel over his head on the road trip somewhere, I can’t remember what game it was, maybe New Orleans. “Draymond actually talked to him about that, to keep an even keel. He wants to be great, and he cares so much, so he’s being a little bit too emotional with the ups and the downs. “You just can’t operate that way. The season will grind you to death if you do. “I love his investment and how much he wants to play and wants to win, but it has got to be more of a day-to-day stable approach, get better, understand how long the season is, and we’re all going to be better off if we keep an even keel.” Yaxel Lendeborg is not the problem for the Golden State Warriors Lendeborg will be the first one to admit that he hasn’t been great for the Warriors lately, but the real problem is their over-reliance on Steph Curry. When the 38-year-old superstar is in the team, the Warriors come out on top more often than not and play like they are one of the contenders. In his absence, however, it has been a different story. The Warriors desperately need Curry back in the side, but the fact that they are so reliant on a 38-year-old is a big problem. Mike Dunleavy Jr. has to find a way to fix that, but whether he can in the middle of the season is an entirely different story. It remains to be seen what will happen to the Warriors, but until Curry comes back, we just can’t see how they will look as good again. technology.title: ChatGPT shrunk down to run on a Super Nintendo
technology.description: If you’ve ever wondered how small an instance of ChatGPT could get, wonder no longer. Someone has actually rigged up a tiny version of the chatbot to run on a Super Nintendo cartridge. Tech journalist and retro tech enthusiast Benj Edwards is responsible for ChatGPT for SNES . He's published it online running in an emulator, complete with SNES-era music and sound effects, and for download as an SNES ROM, too. It’s not a big model, mind you, and performance is thus pretty limited: According to the website, it’s a 2.2 million-parameter offshoot of OpenAI’s GPT-OSS-120b, which was used to develop its training conversations – so in that sense it truly is a ChatGPT that runs on an SNES cartridge. Edwards described it to The Register as a distilled version of the aforementioned open-weight model. There are two options built into ChatGPT for SNES: One that’s purely the model, with every word generated coming right from its tiny little silicon brain, and another that includes a fact book culled from the opening sentences of around 150,000 simple English Wikipedia articles. If you opt to run both versions and ask it the same questions, you’ll notice a massive difference. Given some of the other responses we got while testing, there’s really no good reason to run the base model – memory isn’t really an issue given the basic build is about 4MB and the factbook build is just 19MB. Edwards admits that it’s not the most helpful AI model, either – this is just an experiment after all. “It is not a useful assistant: the model is millions of times smaller than the models behind ChatGPT, knows about 8,000 words, and often gets things wrong, sometimes confidently,” Edwards noted in his writeup. In that sense, it really is vintage AI on vintage hardware. “The fact book can carry mistakes too.” If you have an SNES lying around (lucky you), you can download the ROM from this link. If you want to get it running on an SNES you’ll need a cartridge that allows running of custom ROMs, and that supports Nintendo’s Super FX graphics coprocessor. Cartridges like the FXPak Pro and SD2SNES support it. The factbook version also requires support for the aftermarket Media Streaming Unit 1 (MSU-1), which adds CD-ROM like features to the SNES. MSU-1 is available in both of the flash carts mentioned above. technology.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

"Buying software and data through AWS Marketplace just got easier, for you and for the AI agents working alongside you," said Mya Papolu, product marketing manager for AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at Amazon Web Services, in a blog post this week. "For re:Invent 2026, we’re launching capabilities designed to reduce friction across the buying journey." For a company that has blocked bots from Google, Meta, and OpenAI, and sued Perplexity to keep its AI-encumbered Comet browser away, the openness of AWS Marketplace to agentic commerce invites questions. technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. All three financial firms attributed the compromises to a third-party provider, and while nothing in the stolen files name the vendor, the timing matches up with a Qubole supply-chain campaign disclosed earlier this month by Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders and AI data security company Sentra. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. technology.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
technology.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. The result will be more permission prompts for users of macOS apps that seek access to user data, and the inconvenience of applying for an entitlement from Apple to obtain Full Disk Access for backup software and assistive technologies that use Accessibility APIs. technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: APOD: 2026 November 21 – Voyager’s Neptune
science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 21 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Voyager’s Neptune Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet . Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton , and faint system of rings. From just beyond Neptune’s orbit, the interplanetary perspective looks back toward the Sun, capturing the planet and Triton as thin sunlit crescents . Cirrus clouds and a dark band circle Neptune’s south polar region, with a cloudy vortex above the pole itself . Parts of the very faint ring system along with the three bright ring arcs were first imaged by Voyager during the fly-by, though the faintest segments are modeled in this composited picture. Spanning 7.5 degrees, the background starfield is composed from sky survey data centered on the constellation Camelopardalis, corresponding to the outbound Voyager’s view of the magnificent Neptunian system . science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. But the formula only works if all the zeros always sit on the same vertical line when plotted in a coordinate system where the horizontal axis tracks their real numb

science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.
